title: Output Contest Matches
notes:
Task: Given a power-of-two number n, construct the tournament bracket string by pairing the first and last teams in each round until one match remains.
Idea: Represent teams as strings and repeatedly pair the first remaining team with the last, preserving bracket order.
Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.
Edge cases: n=4 -> ((1,4),(2,3))
Complexity: O(n) time and O(n log n) auxiliary space, subject to output storage.
complexity_reason: Each round creates n/2 fewer bracket strings overall across logarithmically many rounds; the output string contains O(n) team labels and parentheses.

title: Number of Provinces
notes:
Task: Given an n by n adjacency matrix for an undirected graph, return the number of connected components (provinces).
Idea: Start a graph traversal from each unvisited city; each new traversal discovers one province.
Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.
Edge cases: isConnected=[[1,1,0],[1,1,0],[0,0,1]] -> 2
Complexity: O(n²) time and O(n) auxiliary space, subject to output storage.
complexity_reason: The adjacency matrix is scanned at most once per visited city; the visited set and DFS stack hold at most n cities.

title: Student Attendance Record I
approach_name: Count absences and detect late streak
notes:
Task: Return true if a student's attendance string contains fewer than two A characters and never contains three consecutive L characters.
Idea: Count absences and reject any string with a three-character LLL window.
Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.
Edge cases: s="PPALLP" -> true
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary auxiliary space, subject to output storage.
complexity_reason: Counting absences and checking for the forbidden three-character substring take linear time.

title: Optimal Division
notes:
Task: Insert division operators and parentheses into a positive integer array to maximize the result, preserving array order.
Idea: For at least three numbers, the maximum is the first number divided by the quotient of all remaining numbers; this is achieved by grouping the denominator.
Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.
Edge cases: nums=[1000,100,10,2] -> "1000/(100/10/2)"
Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space, subject to output storage.
complexity_reason: The output includes each number once and constructs the parenthesized denominator in linear time and space.

notes:

title: Maximum Depth of N-ary Tree
notes:
Task: Return the maximum number of nodes along a path from the root to any leaf in an N-ary tree; an empty tree has depth zero.
Idea: The depth of a node is one plus the maximum depth among its children.
Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.
Edge cases: root with children [3,2,4] and node 3 having child 5 -> 3
Complexity: O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary space, subject to output storage.
complexity_reason: Each node is visited once; recursion uses stack space proportional to tree height.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
notes:

Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.

Complexity: O(n) expected time and O(n) auxiliary space, subject to output storage.

title: Array Partition
notes:
Task: Pair 2n integers into n pairs to maximize the sum of the smaller value in each pair.
Idea: After sorting, pair adjacent values; the smaller member of each pair is at every even index.
Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.
Edge cases: nums=[1,4,3,2] -> 4
Complexity: O(n log n) time and O(1) auxiliary excluding sort implementation auxiliary space, subject to output storage.
complexity_reason: Sorting dominates; the sum takes linear time and constant additional space beyond the sort.

title: Binary Tree Tilt
notes:

Idea: Postorder DFS computes each subtree sum and accumulates the tilt at each node.
Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.
Edge cases: root=[1,2,3] -> 1
Complexity: O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary space, subject to output storage.
complexity_reason: Each node is processed once and recursive stack space depends on tree height.

title: Reshape the Matrix
approach_name: Map flattened indices to new coordinates
notes:
Task: Reshape a matrix into r rows and c columns without changing the row-major order of elements. If the element count does not match, return the original matrix.
Idea: Map flat index i to old coordinates i/oldColumns and i%oldColumns, and to new coordinates i/c and i%c.
Invariant: Maintain the traversal, count, or prefix state that represents the processed portion of the input.
Edge cases: mat=[[1,2],[3,4]], r=1, c=4 -> [[1,2,3,4]]
Complexity: O(mn) time and O(mn) auxiliary space, subject to output storage.
complexity_reason: Every matrix element is copied once into the reshaped matrix.
